note: Golden vectors for the authentication assurance-level evaluator. Example frameworks are FIXTURE DATA (caller-supplied inputs), never kernel constants: 'nist-example' is modeled on NIST SP 800-63B-4 AAL1-3 and 'eidas-example' on Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502 annex levels, per research/AUTHENTICATOR-ASSURANCE-PIN-2026-10-30.md. No user identifiers, no credentials, no secrets -- inputs are kinds, boolean capabilities and minute intervals only.

vectors.name: eidas_low_password_only
vectors.description: Single knowledge-factor authenticator meets the lowest eIDAS-example level (one factor at low).

output_payload.note: Rates a DECLARED authenticator set and session policy against a caller-supplied, versioned assurance framework -- never a hardcoded one. Every threshold, required factor category and restriction comes from the framework the caller declares; the kernel never interprets a framework it was not given. A criterion the definition cannot express (malformed criterion value) is reported as AAL_DEFINITION_INSUFFICIENT, distinct from AAL_SHORTFALL (declared data failing a well-formed criterion, reported per criterion as {criterion, required, found}) -- the two are never conflated. When the target level is not met, achieved_level falls back to the highest fully-met level below it. Measures declared capabilities only: it does not assert anyone controls any authenticator, and carries no user identifiers.
